rule: Stop for CAPTCHA, Cloudflare, login, 2FA, account switching, payment, permission prompts, or unclear legal, identity, work authorization, sponsorship, or compensation questions.

rule: Do not treat the Greenhouse board list API's updated_at as a posting date; filter candidates by title and location first, then confirm freshness with first_published on the job detail endpoint.

rule: Read the first line of a Workday body before shortlisting a new-grad AI req; the sponsorship exclusion is often stated above the job description rather than in the qualifications.

reason: GlobalFoundries' AI/ML Software Engineer (2026 New College Graduate) req requires expertise in CPU and SoC architecture and MLIR/IREE compiler infrastructure and asks the hire to lead workload-driven architecture strategy, which is not new-grad scope.

rule: On a dry day, the direct company-board sweep is the only source that produces leads, but nearly all of its hits are already tracked; dedupe against job_pool before reading any body.
reason: On 2026-08-21 the sweep returned 89 title-and-location matches across 71 reachable boards and only 3 were new, all of which became the day's pending leads. Both trackers and the Simplify board produced nothing.

rule: Treat a campus or cohort requisition as fresh for its whole recruiting cycle rather than skipping it on first_published; check the interview start date instead.
reason: Five Rings' Campus Full Time 2027 - Software Developer was first published 2026-07-14, five weeks outside the freshness window, but states that interviews begin September 2026, so it is an open 2027 cohort req and not a stale posting.

rule: When a company posts the same role under two start dates, track both rather than folding one into the other, and read both bodies; sibling reqs can differ on compensation disclosure.
reason: Freeform's New Grad December 2026 req lists 125,000-150,000 USD while its otherwise identical New Grad Summer 2027 sibling, screened on 2026-08-20, lists no salary at all. Reading only one would have left an open compensation question that the other req answers.

rule: Read qualification lists for PERM labor-certification phrasing such as 'N months of experience in job offered'; flag the lead rather than skipping it, because the req may be tied to an existing employee's filing.

rule: When a posting states a graduation requirement in its title and a different one in its body, the body governs, but record the conflict and hand the decision to the user before applying.
reason: Applied Intuition's Cybersecurity Software Engineer req on 2026-09-03 is titled New Grad (December 2027) and requires graduating December 2026 in the body. The body's date is inside the candidate's window and the title's is not, so the two readings give opposite classifications.

rule: Read Breezy postings from the board feed at https://<company>.breezy.hr/json, which carries salary, remote details, and published date; the posting page itself renders through JavaScript and returns only placeholder tokens.
reason: Climavision's page returned 76 characters of template placeholders on 2026-09-03 while the JSON feed returned the full record including the 75,000-90,000 USD band that the screen turned on.

rule: Read Eightfold-hosted postings from https://<company>.eightfold.ai/api/apply/v2/jobs/<id>?domain=<company domain>, which returns the full job_description as JSON.
reason: Boston Scientific's Software Engineer I req on 2026-09-03 was screened this way, and the endpoint carried both the no-sponsorship statement and the prior-internship requirement that decided it.

rule: Read iCIMS postings by appending the mobile query string to the /job URL: ?mobile=true&width=600&height=500&bga=true&needsRedirect=false&jan1offset=-300&jun1offset=-240. The plain URL renders through JavaScript and yields almost no text.
reason: HealthEdge's Associate Software Engineer returned 20 characters of extractable text from the plain iCIMS URL on 2026-09-05 and 6,523 characters from the mobile view, including the Bachelor's requirement and the 80,000-100,000 USD band the screen turned on. This narrows the 2026-09-02 rule that grouped iCIMS with Oracle Cloud, metacareers, and Avature as source-limited: iCIMS is readable, the other three are still not.

rule: Workday CXS is readable per tenant, not universally: build the endpoint as https://<host>/wday/cxs/<tenant>/<site>/job/<path> and expect some tenants to refuse it. Treat a 403 as a browser-pass item rather than as a broken query.
reason: Seven of eight Workday postings screened on 2026-09-05 returned full bodies this way, including Cadence, Morgan Stanley, HP, and GEICO. GlobalFoundries returned 403 permission denied on the same construction, so its 2027 New College Graduate req was recorded as an unscreened Pending. Distinguishing a per-tenant refusal from a malformed query is the 2026-08-30 lesson applied to a second source.

rule: A Simplify board row marked with the closed-application lock carries no apply link; record it as Skipped for a closed application rather than chasing the posting.
reason: DoorDash's Software Engineer 1 - Entry-Level appeared on 2026-09-05 across five Tier 1 locations, the best-placed row of the day on title and level, with the lock in place of an apply link. The board legend defines the lock as 'Job application is closed'.

rule: Discount duplicate requisitions from a single employer before reading the day's untracked count; boards list the same req under multiple ATS tenants, including employers' own test tenants.
reason: On 2026-09-05 the untracked count of 74 included four National Information Solutions Cooperative rows for one opening, three of them under a 'testnisc' board token, plus Cadence, HP, Kion Group, Applied Materials, Canadian Tire, and Bank of Montreal each listed twice under two tenants. Eleven rows for five openings.

rule: When a posting names a graduation month at the edge of the candidate's window rather than inside it, keep it Pending and record that eligibility narrows to that month; do not skip, because the skip rule requires the requirement to fall wholly outside the window.
reason: ID.me's Summer 2027 req on 2026-09-05 asks for graduating May/June 2027. The candidate's window runs December 2026 through May 2027, so the two overlap only at May 2027. Neither the skip branch nor the 2026-09-02 term-range branch covers a partial overlap.

rule: When a body requires C++ proficiency but the title does not say C++, the skip rule does not fire; flag the row for the user rather than deciding it silently.
reason: Cadence's new college grad req on 2026-09-05 states the candidate must be proficient in Python and C++, in a role otherwise on target at 101,500-188,500 USD in Tier 1 San Jose with a December 2026 grad date. The rule is written against titles only, and the same question has been open on Five Rings since it was first raised.

rule: Sponsorship and citizenship walls, not fit, are the dominant cause of loss; when a lead is otherwise clean, read the authorization line before anything else.
reason: Eight of the eighteen tracked skips on 2026-09-05 turned on work authorization: Garner Health, New Relic, GEICO, Huntington Bank, and PayPal on sponsorship, Self Financial, Ontic, and Analytical Mechanics Associates on citizenship. Garner Health was an Associate title at 150,000 USD in Tier 1 New York City with no experience bar, lost on a single closing sentence.

rule: Normalize a posting URL by stripping only tracking params (utm_*, ref, gh_src, src) and keeping the rest sorted; never strip the whole query string.
reason: Several employers put the requisition id in the query string (nuro.ai/careersitem?gh_jid=, m1technology.com/careers?gh_jid=, smxtech.com/careers?gh_jid=). Splitting on '?' collapsed all of an employer's postings into one key, which hid the live Nuro ML Infrastructure Platform lead from the queue and mis-flagged Nuro Software Engineer, Performance - New Grad as archived without any user action. Fixed in dashboard-ui/src/App.tsx and vite.config.ts on 2026-09-05; the write-back shares the function, so the same collision was corrupting job_pool.csv, not just the display.

rule: When a lead disappears from the dashboard, check the archive-key collision before concluding the queue is genuinely empty; a row can be hidden with archived=false.
reason: On 2026-09-05 the dashboard showed zero active US leads. Two causes were stacked: the region toggle was left on the empty China track, and the URL collision above hid the one remaining Nuro lead. Cross-checking job_pool.csv against applied_archive.csv finds the second kind: a row flagged archived=true with no matching applied_archive entry was never archived by the user.
